title: How a gas chills your food

segments.text: A fluid inside your fridge acts like a shapeshifter.
It flips between gas and liquid.
Inside the fridge, it starts as a low-pressure gas.
It rushes into a tiny tube.
There, it evaporates into a cloud.
As it evaporates, it pulls heat from the air.
This removes warmth from your leftovers.
That is what chills your food.
The evaporated gas then travels to the compressor.
The cycle repeats to keep the fridge cold.
Evaporation absorbs heat from the air.
The refrigerant starts as a low-pressure gas.
